title: US: DMCA 512(c) notice (only if you own the copyright) + TAKE IT DOWN Act note + state law note
checklist: Decide which section applies: Section A only if YOU own the copyright in the original photo or video that was manipulated; Section B only for intimate imagery; delete the sections that do not apply.
Replace every [PLACEHOLDER] in brackets with your own details.
Do not send a DMCA notice unless you own (or are authorised by the owner of) the copyright: knowingly false notices can make you liable for damages (17 U.S.C. 512(f)).
Find the platform's designated DMCA agent (its copyright page or the U.S. Copyright Office DMCA Designated Agent Directory).
For intimate imagery, use the platform's TAKE IT DOWN Act / non-consensual intimate imagery removal form.
Attach the VeriLoop evidence bundle (bundle.zip) and the signed audit PDF; keep screenshots with URL, date and time.
Check your state's laws on non-consensual intimate imagery and deepfakes with a lawyer or victim-support organisation.
Have a lawyer verify the cited provisions before filing. VeriLoop never sends this draft.
filing_instructions: Section A (DMCA): send to the platform's designated agent; a notice must contain the six elements of 17 U.S.C. 512(c)(3)(A), all included below.

Section B (TAKE IT DOWN Act, enacted May 19, 2025): covered platforms must run a notice-and-removal process and remove a validly reported non-consensual intimate depiction, including a computer-generated digital forgery, within 48 hours; the platform obligations apply from May 19, 2026.
Section C: state statutes on non-consensual intimate imagery and on sexual or election deepfakes vary by state; some give a private right of action.
If you are in danger or being extorted, contact local law enforcement; you can also report online crime to the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (ic3.gov).
